title: How to Read a PhD Job Advert: Funding, Eligibility and Application Steps
seoTitle: How to Read a PhD Advert: Eligibility and Funding
seoDescription: Read a PhD advert for essential criteria, research fit, funding and submission rules, then map your real evidence to the project requirements.
intro: Read a PhD advert as a set of conditions to check. Identify the scientific question, essential qualifications, funding package, location and submission process before investing time in the application.
description:
Identify what is fixed and what is open

A PhD advertisement can describe a defined funded project, a broad doctoral programme or an opportunity to propose your own research. Read the project description and application instructions together. A broad title does not prove that every topic is available, and a specific title does not tell you how much the methods can be adjusted. Ask the named contact where the advert leaves a material question unanswered.

Start with the institution's original vacancy page. A job board or discovery service can help locate it, but the host or funder provides the governing application instructions. Save the vacancy reference, closing date and relevant linked guidance. If a page changes while you prepare, you will have a record of the version you used.

Separate essential and desirable criteria

Read qualification requirements exactly as written. Note the degree level, subject, grade or equivalence guidance and whether the qualification must be complete by application or the proposed start. Funding eligibility can add citizenship, residence or other conditions. Do not assume the academic programme and the scholarship use identical rules.

Make a two-column evidence list. Put each essential criterion on one side and your supporting evidence on the other. Then repeat the exercise for desirable skills. If an essential requirement is unclear, ask how the policy applies to your actual qualification. If a desirable technique is new to you, explain related preparation and a credible learning need rather than claiming proficiency.

Read the financial offer independently

Financial detailQuestion the advert should help you answer
TuitionWhich fee status and how much of the fee are covered?
IncomeIs the payment a salary or stipend, and what period does it cover?
DurationHow many months of support are guaranteed?
Other costsWhich research, immigration or relocation costs remain yours?
ConditionsAre review, renewal or employment obligations attached?

An advert welcoming international applicants does not itself establish full international tuition coverage. Ask the funding office about any difference between a stated home-fee contribution and the applicable international fee. For employment, check the pay agreement, contract percentage and salary basis. Compare the full package rather than a headline number.

Investigate supervision without relying on stereotypes

Read relevant papers to understand the group's methods and current questions. Look for a connection you can explain from your own preparation. Group size alone does not tell you how often supervision happens, and a familiar university name does not establish access to the equipment your project needs.

Ask about supervision arrangements, co-supervision and the first research milestones where appropriate. A centrally recruited programme may allocate a supervisor later, so the absence of a named supervisor is not automatically suspicious. Use the programme structure and official contact route to understand how the match is made.

Check the application mechanics

Record every required document, its limit and its submission method. A cover letter, research statement and proposal can answer different questions. Do not submit a full proposal when the advert asks only for a response to defined criteria. Check whether references are requested with the initial application or at a later stage.

Convert the deadline to your local time and identify any earlier departmental nomination date. Submit through the official route and retain confirmation. An email to a supervisor may be an enquiry rather than an application, even when the supervisor responds positively.

Turn the reading into a decision

Before drafting, explain the opportunity in four sentences: the research question, the preparation it requires, the funding available and the process for applying. If one sentence depends on an assumption, identify the source or ask a precise question. This prevents several days of writing for a position whose essential conditions you have not established.

Do not try to make your experience match every word in the advert. Select your strongest evidence for the requirements that matter and explain it accurately. Keep uncertain future work separate from achievements. A measured application is easier to defend in an interview than one built from copied terminology.

Translate the advert into evidence you can submit

Copy each essential criterion into a working checklist and put your evidence beside it. If the evidence is missing, decide whether the advert permits equivalent preparation or whether you need clarification. Keep desirable criteria separate so that you neither exclude yourself unnecessarily nor treat an essential condition as optional.

Check that the application route is real and complete. A contact email may be for enquiries while formal applications belong in a portal. Save the vacancy reference, deadline and submitted confirmation. If the advert links to funding guidance, read it rather than assuming the headline summarises every condition.

Advert detailPractical action
Required qualificationCompare the exact degree and subject requirement with your record.
Research methodsIdentify one real example of relevant preparation.
FundingConfirm fee coverage, maintenance and the guaranteed period.
DocumentsFollow the requested formats and limits.
SubmissionUse the official route and check receipt.

Should I apply if I lack one desirable skill?

Assess the essential requirements first. If you meet them, explain your relevant preparation and the realistic training need without claiming a skill you do not have.

Retain a short decision record

Before applying, write down why the project belongs on your shortlist and what would make you decline an offer. Include the scientific question, the evidence you can contribute, essential financial conditions and any practical constraint. This helps you compare later offers without being distracted by a changed headline or a familiar institution name. If a condition is unresolved, give it an owner and a question: for example, the funding office confirming international fee coverage. Keep academic discussions and administrative confirmations together while recording who supplied each answer. The record should distinguish a formal commitment from an informal expectation, so that an encouraging conversation does not quietly become a guaranteed term in your plan.

Official sources and further reading

Requirements and policies should be checked for your programme and application date. Sources checked on 19 October 2026.

  • Oxford: graduate application requirements
  • Cambridge: postgraduate entry requirements

  • Applying for a PhD Without a Master's: Check the Programme Rules
